verdict: Spend pulled back this week; tracking gaps are being closed before scale-up.
narrative: Google Ads spend totaled $1,317.43 over the last 28 days, down 26% from the prior week — driven by the Local Services campaign exhausting its daily budget mid-day on multiple occasions rather than a deliberate reduction. Your Google Business Profile drew 115 actions this period, including 31 calls, showing that organic demand remains active even as paid slowed. Lead-count tracking is currently broken at the attribution level — 80 contacts and 13 recorded Google conversions exist in the system, but they are not connecting properly, so cost-per-lead cannot be calculated right now; that fix is in progress. Several important milestones land by August 31st — the Homer Glen branch page, financing page, and review campaign all go live — and heating campaigns are scheduled to turn on October 1st, setting up the busiest part of your season.

watch_item.issue: Ad spend is hitting budget limits mid-day, causing zero-spend gaps on 9 of the last 28 days — meaning you are going dark during hours when customers are searching.
watch_item.fix: Budget pacing is being reviewed this week ahead of the September 1st Local Services re-enable, so spend flows consistently through the day rather than stopping short.
